items.title: Systemic two-column TOC corruption -- most of OR.S02 through OR.S16 titles/parenting are wrong
items.summary: The printed Toronto Notes TOC for this chapter (raw OCR of pdf 1089) is a genuine two-column layout: left column runs Acronyms->Basic Anatomy Review->Fractures General Principles->Articular Cartilage->Orthopedic X-Ray Imaging->Orthopedic Emergencies->Shoulder->Humerus->Elbow->Radius and Ulna Shaft Fractures->Wrist->Hand->Spine->Pelvis->Hip; right column runs Femur->Knee->Patella->Tibia->Ankle->Foot->Pediatric Orthopedics->Bone Tumours->Common Medications->Landmark Orthopedic Trials->References. The automated toc_inventory.json extraction read both columns as a single interleaved stream, merging left-column row N with right-column row N into one garbled node title for most of the chapter (e.g. OR.S10 'Rotator Cuff Disease Ankle'), silently dropped entire right-column sections/children that had no same-row-index left-column partner to merge into (Fractures General Principles, Articular Cartilage, Orthopedic X-Ray Imaging, the Orthopedic Emergencies and Shoulder section headers themselves, Femur, most of Knee's 8 children, Tibial Shaft Fracture, Achilles tendon pathology, Plantar Fasciitis, Bunions -- 5 of these are also independently flagged UNRESOLVED in research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json), and mis-parented three real Spine children (Fractures of the Spine, Cervical Spine, Thoracolumbar Spine) under the unrelated References section. Resolved via raw OCR of the TOC page plus ~25 spot-verification reads of body pages across the full pdf 1089-1141 range, cross-checked against the printed two-column structure and heading-adjacency at every point checked; no instance of my reconstructed left/right column ordering conflicted with body-page content. Full correction and per-unit citations are in study_units.json's methodology_note and each unit's structural_rationale.
items.recommended_action: Reviewer should spot-check a handful of the 75 reconstructed study units against the source PDF page images (not just raw OCR text, which was the only evidence used here) -- particularly the Femur/Knee/Foot units sourced entirely from synthetic UNCATALOGUED ids, since no toc_inventory.json node exists for them at all. Coordinator may also wish to log a toc_inventory.json extraction-pipeline defect report: this chapter's corruption pattern (genuine two-column TOC read as a single stream) is categorically different from the single-heading-pair merges seen in prior chapters (OP, OB, NS) and may indicate other chapters with two-column TOC layouts warrant a similar full re-check.

items.title: Hand section has no distinct body content beyond a Plastic Surgery cross-reference
items.summary: OR.S04's captured title 'Hand' co-locates with 'Spine' per merged_duplicate_headings (both real TOC headings on the same row/page, OR25/pdf1113). Raw OCR of pdf 1113 shows the preceding Wrist and Thumb CMC Joint Arthritis section's treatment content ends with an explicit 'see Plastic Surgery, PL24' redirect, and no distinct 'Hand'-titled clinical content (fractures, infections, etc.) was located between that redirect and 'Fractures of the Spine'. Represented as a thin CROSS_DISCIPLINE cross-reference unit rather than an UNRESOLVED gap, since the redirect itself is the substantive finding.
items.recommended_action: Reviewer should confirm against the source PDF (pdf page 1113, TN OR25) that no substantive Hand-specific clinical content (e.g. finger fractures, hand infections) was missed between the CMC arthritis content and the Spine section -- the raw-OCR text alone does not rule out a short 'Hand' subheading with content that the OCR extraction dropped entirely (as happened with several Foot/Knee headings in this same chapter).

items.title: Achilles Tendon Pathology: TOC says 'Rupture', body heading reads 'Tendonitis'
items.summary: The raw TOC OCR (pdf 1089) reads the relevant right-column heading as 'chilles Tendon Rupture' (garbled 'Achilles Tendon Rupture'), but raw OCR of pdf 1131-1132 (OR43-OR44) body-confirms the actual printed heading is 'Achilles Tendonitis' -- whose content nonetheless explicitly discusses rupture mechanism/site as its opening line. Represented as a single combined 'Achilles Tendon Pathology (Tendonitis and Rupture)' unit under the body-confirmed title rather than assuming either OCR reading is authoritative on its own.
items.recommended_action: Reviewer should confirm against the source PDF whether OR43-44 in fact contains two adjacent headings (Achilles Tendonitis, then a separate Achilles Tendon Rupture heading) that raw-text OCR compressed into one, in which case the unit should be split into two per the OP.S03/OB.S07 compound-heading-split precedent.

items.title: Cauda equina / osteomyelitis / spine content substantially overlaps Neurosurgery and Infectious Diseases
items.summary: Several units carry explicit in-text redirects to sister chapters (Fractures of the Spine -> 'see Neurosurgery, NS39'; Cervical Spine's acute-injury content -> 'see Neurosurgery, NS38'; Hand -> 'see Plastic Surgery, PL24') or substantial thematic overlap without an explicit redirect (Cauda Equina Syndrome with Neurosurgery's cord-compression objectives; Osteomyelitis with Infectious Diseases' bone/joint infection content). Per project instruction (matching the OB/OP precedent), PRIMARY_OWNER/CROSS_LINK/DISTINCT_CONTEXT designation is deferred to a later global cross-chapter audit; these are recorded here as thin CROSS_DISCIPLINE-flavored units retaining only the orthopedic-recognition/referral angle.
items.recommended_action: Defer to global cross-chapter ownership audit; no chapter-local action required.

items.title: Multiple study units carry only WEAK MCC evidence or are mapped only to broad Trauma/arthralgia objectives
items.summary: A full-registry search-mcc-objectives sweep for 'fracture', 'osteoarthritis', 'compartment syndrome', 'septic', 'arthritis', 'swelling', 'immobil', and related orthopedic terms returned zero or near-zero direct matches. The MCC Objectives registry has no orthopedic-disease-specific presentation list; nearly all fracture/dislocation content in this chapter is instead mapped as DIRECT/COMPONENT against the broad trauma family (109 Trauma, 109-3 Bone or joint injury, 109-11 Nerve injury, 109-13 Spinal trauma, 109-15 Vascular injury) or the arthralgia/pain family (50-1 through 50-5), and pediatric orthopedic conditions against 20 (Limp in children) or 74 (Periodic health encounter, for DDH/scoliosis screening). This mirrors the OP chapter's finding that the registry lacks disease-specific objectives for a high-prevalence specialty domain, consistent with project accuracy rules (WEAK/UNCERTAIN used rather than fabricated DIRECT evidence).
items.recommended_action: None required at this stage -- consistent with project accuracy rules (no invented MCC IDs; WEAK used where evidence is indirect). Coordinator may wish to note, in a future cross-chapter registry-gap audit, that the MCC Objectives Online registry lacks dedicated objectives for numerous high-prevalence orthopedic diagnoses (fracture subtypes, osteoarthritis, ligament injury) despite the general Trauma/Bone-or-joint-injury objectives existing to anchor them.
